etymologies.etymologyHTML: From addict +‎ -ion; compare (Latin) addictio (“an adjudging, an award”).

definitions.definition: (medicine) A state that is characterized by compulsive drug use or compulsive engagement in rewarding behavior, despite negative consequences.[1][2]

quote.citation: 2019, Thy Art is Murder, Chemical Christ:
quote.text: Do your lethal addictions to self-prescriptions numb the ache of the darkest days?

definitions.definition: The state of being addicted; devotion; inclination.
A habit or practice that damages, jeopardizes or shortens one's life but when ceased causes trauma.
A pathological relationship to mood altering experience that has life damaging consequences.

quote.citation: 1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Life of Henry the Fift”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene i]:
quote.text: His addiction was to courses vain.
